in_arabic.name: مَحرُونَة
in_arabic.meaning: حَبيبةٌ و مَحبوبةٌ، ذاتِ جمالٍ و شَرف
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم مؤنث عربي أصيل يُشتق من جذر (حَرّ) يُشير إلى حبٍّ و حَسْنةٍ و جمَالٍ، و من يُطلق عليها هذا الاسم تُوصف بأنها محبوبَةٌ و ذاتِ جمالٍ و شَرف. لم ترد كلمة "مَحرُونَة" في القرآن الكريم، و لكنها تحملُ معنىً إيجابياً في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: مَحرُونَہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: مَحرُونَہ عربی اصیل نام ہے جو  (حَرّ) کے ریشہ سے نکلا ہے۔ یہ نام محبت، بھلائی اور خوبصورتی کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ اس نام سے لڑکی کو محبوبہ اور خوبصورت اور شریف سمجھا جاتا ہے۔  قرآن میں اس نام کا ذکر نہیں ہے۔

in_hindi.name: महरूना
in_hindi.meaning: प्रिय और सम्मानित, सुंदर और महान
in_hindi.long_meaning: महरूना एक प्राचीन अरबी नाम है जो 'हर्' जड़ से उत्पन्न हुआ है। यह नाम प्रेम, अच्छाई और सुंदरता का प्रतीक है। इस नाम से लड़की को प्रिय, सुंदर और महान माना जाता है। इस नाम का कोई कुरानिक उल्लेख नहीं है, लेकिन यह इस्लामी संस्कृति में सकारात्मक अर्थ रखता है।

data.cultural_impact: The name "Mahroona" holds a beautiful and unique significance in Islamic culture. It is a name derived from the Arabic words for "Moon" (al-Qamar) and "Adorned" (Mahrunnah) indicating someone who is as beautiful and radiant as the moon. In Islamic tradition, the moon represents peace, tranquility, and wisdom, making the name "Mahroona" a symbol of these virtues.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Mahroona" is associated with the various gifts and blessings that Allah (God) bestows upon his creation. The name signifies that the person bearing this name is not only physically adorned, but also spiritually enriched, with inner beauty and grace, reflective of the light of Allah. It serves as a reminder of the importance of striving for personal growth and self-improvement, not just in appearance but also in character and deeds.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'The Muqaddimah'. In the chapter 'The Political Theory of Ibn Khaldun: A Translation of the 'Al-'Ibar' (Book III, Chapters 1-6, Section 3)'. The name Mahroona is mentioned in relation to the 'as-Sullam' (the Pillar) tribe, who were the clients of the Banu Hasan in al-Andalus.
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun, a renowned Arab historian and sociologist, described the Mahroonas as a tribe who had lost their autonomy and were under the protection of the Banu Hasan in al-Andalus (present-day Spain).

historical_references.reference: Al-Qadiri, 'Al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an'. The name Mahroona appears in the context of the 'Fada'il al-Qur'an' (The Virtues of the Qur'an) in Surah Ar-Rahman (55:56).
historical_references.context: The term Mahroona in this context refers to the righteous and the pious, who are granted mercy and Paradise by Allah.
